Traditional Irish Soda Bread

Served at: Saint Patrick's Day

Serves 8-10Prep 15 minCook 45-55 min

Irish Soda Bread is a quintessential part of Saint Patrick's Day celebrations, offering a simple yet hearty accompaniment to festive meals. Its characteristic dense crumb and slightly tangy flavor, thanks to buttermilk and baking soda, make it a beloved staple that evokes the warmth of Irish hospitality.

Ingredients

  • 4 cups (480 g) all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
  • 1 teaspoon (5 g) baking soda
  • 1 teaspoon (5 g) salt
  • 1 tablespoon (15 g) granulated sugar (optional, for a slightly sweeter loaf)
  • 4 tablespoons (56 g) unsalted butter, cold and cut into small pieces
  • 1 3/4 cups (420 ml) buttermilk, plus more for brushing

Method

  1. Preheat your oven to 425°F (220°C) and lightly flour a baking sheet or line with parchment paper.
  2. In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the flour, baking soda, salt, and sugar (if using).
  3. Add the cold butter pieces to the dry ingredients and, using your fingertips, rub the butter into the flour mixture until it resembles coarse crumbs.
  4. Make a well in the center of the flour mixture and pour in the buttermilk.
  5. Using one hand, mix the ingredients with your fingers, drawing the flour from the sides into the center until a shaggy dough forms. Do not overmix.
  6. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and gently knead for just 1-2 minutes, bringing it together into a round, slightly flattened loaf.
  7. Transfer the dough to the prepared baking sheet.
  8. Using a sharp knife, score a deep 'X' into the top of the loaf, about halfway through the dough.
  9. Brush the top of the loaf with a little extra buttermilk for a golden crust.
  10. Bake for 15 minutes at 425°F (220°C), then reduce the oven temperature to 375°F (190°C) and continue baking for another 30-40 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown and the loaf sounds hollow when tapped on the bottom.
  11. Let the soda bread cool on a wire rack before slicing and serving.

Tips

  • For a richer flavor, use full-fat buttermilk. If you don't have buttermilk, you can make a substitute by adding 1 tablespoon (15 ml) of lemon juice or white vinegar to a liquid measuring cup, then filling the rest with regular milk to 1 3/4 cups (420 ml) and letting it sit for 5 minutes.
  • Avoid overmixing the dough; this is key to keeping soda bread tender. A light hand ensures a soft crumb.
  • Serve warm with butter, jam, or alongside a hearty Irish stew for a complete Saint Patrick's Day meal.
